item.title: i-have-adhd plugin provides ADHD-friendly output for coding assistants
item.description:
i-have-adhd plugin provides ADHD-friendly output for coding assistants

The i-have-adhd plugin was released to make AI-powered coding assistants more accessible for users with ADHD. The plugin reformats outputs as numbered action steps, leads with the next action, and avoids unnecessary tangents or pleasantries.

🧩 How it works

The plugin modifies how a coding assistant responds by:

  • Breaking tasks into numbered steps
  • Leading with immediate actions
  • Ending with one concrete next step
  • Making test failures visible
  • Using matter-of-fact error messages

⚙️ Key details

The plugin is available as a skill that can be installed from https://github.com/ayghri/i-have-adhd. Refer to the repo’s AGENTS.md for installation instructions.

Action Command
Uninstall current plugin claude plugin uninstall i-have-adhd
Remove from marketplace claude plugin marketplace remove i-have-adhd
Add forked version claude plugin marketplace add <your-username>/i-have-adhd
Install specific fork claude plugin install i-have-adhd@i-have-adhd

🚀 Availability

The plugin can be installed immediately from the GitHub repository. The instructions require forking, editing skills/i-have-adhd/SKILL.md, then swapping your copy in.

💡 Why it matters

The approach is loosely based on The Adult ADHD Tool Kit by J. Russell Ramsay and Anthony L. Rostain, but adapted for how an LLM should respond rather than human daily organization. The output is ADHD-friendly—no diagnosis needed—and stops coding agents from burying answers in verbose explanations.

#ADHD #AI-assistant #plugins #accessibility

Source: ayghri/i-have-adhd

item.title: open-computer-use expands platform support and adds macOS Locked Use
item.description:
open-computer-use expands platform support and adds macOS Locked Use

open-computer-use, an open‑source Computer Use service wrapped as MCP, has expanded its platform support and added a macOS locked‑use feature.

🔍 Overview

  • open-computer-use is an open‑source Computer Use service wrapped as MCP.
  • Inspired by OpenAI’s Codex Computer Use.
  • Built on Accessibility to create non‑intrusive CUA.

🧩 How It Works

  • Any AI agent or MCP client can run Computer Use on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
  • Gemini CLI connects through MCP to run full Computer Use actions.
  • In Codex App and Codex CLI, it matches official experience.

⚙️ Key Details

Installation

  • Install the skill directly.
  • Install for Codex.
  • Install for Claude Code.
  • Update an existing global install, including Codex install created above.
  • Manually download and install the open‑computer‑use skill.

Usage

  • Call a single Computer Use tool and print the MCP‑style JSON result.
  • Run a sequence in one process to reuse element_index state.
  • Sequence sleeps 1s between successful operations by default.

Permissions

  • On macOS, run once and grant Accessibility and Screen Recording.
  • Windows and Linux do not require this step.
  • Check permissions; onboarding opens only when missing.
  • macOS: query permission JSON without opening onboarding.

Configuration

  • ocu supports global configuration starting with version 1.0.0.
  • Default configuration file: ~/.config/ocu/config.json.

Locked Use (macOS)

  • Locked Use is now supported on macOS.
  • OCU temporarily unlocks the Mac after it has been locked so the agent can continue working.
  • Protective services such as a full‑screen shield are in place during use.
  • See the Locked Use guide for setup, installed components, and permissions.

Runtime Requirements (macOS)

Requirement Detail
macOS version 14.0 or later
Permissions Accessibility & Screen Recording
Steps Run once to grant permissions

🚀 Availability

  • Running on Linux.
  • macOS runtime requires macOS 14.0+.
  • Windows and Linux require no special permissions.

💡 Why it Matters

  • Has become one of the most useful workflows for nearly 100 % AI‑generated projects.
  • Built on open source, enabling quick setup with the harness template.
  • Offers a non‑intrusive, accessibility‑based solution for Computer Use across major OSes.

For more on the methodology behind this project, see the post at https://www.ifuryst.com/blog/2026/speedrunning-the-ai-era/

#OpenAI #ComputerUse #AIAgents #macOS #Accessibility

Source: iFurySt/open-computer-use

item.title: Memorial Coliseum Ticketing, Parking, and Accessibility Guidelines Updated
item.description:
Memorial Coliseum Ticketing, Parking, and Accessibility Guidelines Updated

The Memorial Coliseum has released a set of detailed guidelines covering show hours, ticket verification, parking rates, accessibility accommodations, photography rules, and child admission policies.

📅 Show Hours & Admission

  • Shows run from 10 AM to 4 PM.
  • Children 3 years and under are free for most events.
  • Children under 2 years are free unless a separate seat is requested.
  • Rules for children can vary by event; verify the individual event for specifics.

🎟️ Ticketing Details

  • Ticket office phone: (260) 483‑1111.
  • Doors open 2 hours prior to the event.
  • To pick up tickets, present one of the following:
    • Photo ID
    • Confirmation number
    • Credit card used for the purchase

🚗 Parking Rates

Parking Area Rate per Vehicle
Main Lot $8.00
Preferred Lot $12.00
Buses, RVs, Limos $16.00

♿ Accessibility

  • Accessible seating is available at all purchase points.
  • Seats are reserved for sight‑ or hearing‑impaired patrons.
  • Special amenities include hearing devices and sign‑language interpreters.
  • For assistance, contact the MidWest America Ticket Office at 260‑483‑1111.
  • TTY assistance is reachable at 260‑480‑2108.

📸 Camera & Recording Policy

  • Still‑photo cameras are permitted for certain events.
  • Video cameras and recording devices are prohibited for most events.
  • For event‑specific policies, visit www.memorialcoliseum.com.

📞 Contact Information

  • General ticketing inquiries: (260) 483‑1111.
  • Special‑amenities requests: (260) 483‑1111.
  • TTY machine: (260) 480‑2108.

All information reflects the latest guidelines as of October 10, 2026.

#Ticketing #Accessibility #VenuePolicies

Source: Tickets, Live at Allen County War Memorial Coliseum, Fort Wayne on Oct 11, 2026 | Consequence Live

item.title: Google launches Guided Vision in Gemini Live for real‑time audio descriptions on Android
item.description:
Google launches Guided Vision in Gemini Live for real‑time audio descriptions on Android

Google’s Guided Vision feature debuted today in the Gemini Live app on compatible Android devices, providing real‑time audio descriptions of anything pointed at with the phone’s camera.

🔍 Overview

  • Guided Vision works when you share your camera in Gemini Live.
  • It delivers spoken information about small text, surroundings, objects, and details on specific items.
  • Users can ask follow‑up questions, such as reading an expiration date.

🧩 How it works

  • The phone’s camera feed is processed by Google’s Gemini AI, which generates audio cues to help line up the shot if the target is off‑frame.
  • The system is designed for people who are blind, have low vision, or need situational assistance, similar to Apple’s VoiceOver Live Recognition.

⚙️ Key details

  • Reading fine print – the AI can read small text and fine print.
  • Object identification – it can find or identify objects in the scene.
  • Follow‑up queries – users can ask additional questions about what they see.
  • Audio alignment cues – Gemini provides cues to adjust the camera view.
  • Safety disclaimer – Google advises not to rely on Guided Vision for navigation, safe‑travel guidance, obstacle detection, or as a substitute for a cane or mobility aid.

🚀 Availability

  • Integrated in the Gemini Live app.
  • Also available through Google TalkBack.
  • Can be enabled via an accessibility shortcut in the Settings app on Android 9 and above, following recent Pixel updates.

💡 Why it matters

Guided Vision extends AI‑powered visual assistance to Android users, offering a new way for low‑vision individuals to access information about their environment without additional hardware.

#Google #Accessibility #AI #GuidedVision

Source: Google’s new Guided Vision feature can help you read the fine print

item.title: University Startups Launches Trinity AI to Assist Students with Disability Transition Planning
item.description:
University Startups Launches Trinity AI to Assist Students with Disability Transition Planning

Trinity is a conversational AI solution developed by University Startups to assist students with disabilities in taking ownership of their postsecondary and Individualized Education Program (IEP) planning.

🧩 How it works

University Startups utilized g/d/n/a to build a fully serverless architecture on AWS. The system utilizes a multi-agent solution powered by Amazon Bedrock and Claude 3.5 Sonnet to provide targeted guidance.

The architecture employs a hierarchical six-agent system:

Agent Function
Orchestrator Agent Reads student conversation, selects the right path, sequences agents, and consolidates final output
College Agent Recommends 4-year universities and community colleges from an over 30,000 record Knowledge Base
Employment Agent Matches jobs and career pathways from an over 1,000 occupation Knowledge Base
Training Agent Recommends vocational programs and certifications

⚙️ Key details

The platform includes accessibility features such as Amazon Polly for text-to-speech and Amazon Transcribe for speech-to-text. Data security is maintained through compliance with HIPAA and FERPA standards, while Amazon Bedrock Guardrails are used for content filtering and hallucination reduction.

🚀 Availability

Trinity reached educators and students across more than a dozen U.S. states within its first year. International expansion into Saudi Arabia and Kuwait is now underway.

#ArtificialIntelligence #EdTech #AWS #Accessibility #SpecialEducation

Source: Trinity: Agentic AI-powered transition planning for students with disabilities | Amazon Web Services
